product.olivetti-m24sp.summary: The desktop M24 variant that raises the 8086 clock to 10 MHz and removes memory wait states.
product.olivetti-m24sp.history: The M24 SP had already been presented at SICOB in Paris when Computerwoche reported on it on 11 October 1985; on 22 November the magazine announced availability in Austria. It expanded Olivetti’s professional range alongside the M24 and the transportable M21. Sperimentare names Ing. C. Olivetti & C. S.p.A. as manufacturer and published an Italian price of 9,600,000 lire excluding VAT in June 1986, with 640 KB, one floppy drive, a 20 MB disk and a monochrome monitor. This price postdates the presentation; it is not a launch price.
product.olivetti-m24sp.warning: Historical sheet under research; no dedicated M24 SP validation or creation profile.
product.olivetti-m24sp.technical.configu: Offers varied by market and date. Computerwoche describes 512 KB and 20 MB in Austria in November 1985; Sperimentare lists 640 KB and 20 MB in Italy in June 1986. The German report of August 1986 presents the 20 MB disk as new: both reports are retained without inferring a simultaneous worldwide change.
product.olivetti-m24sp.technical.memory: Memory keeps pace with the faster processor. Olivetti’s guide specifies 10 MHz, 120 ns RAM and zero wait states for the SP, versus 8 MHz, 150 ns and one wait state for M24/M21. It identifies SP boards BA801 and BA177 with a capacity of 640 KB.
product.olivetti-m24sp.technical.board: Jumpers adapt the floppy controller and coprocessor to the configuration. On BA801/BA177, G open enables the floppy controller and closed disables it; H–1 selects 8 MHz for the 8087 and H–2 selects 10 MHz. These are not CPU speed selectors.
product.olivetti-m24sp.technical.firmwar: BIOS revisions help identify the board, but do not authenticate a dump. The guide lists SP revisions 1.36H PBFW / 1.36L PBFV and 1.43H PQBK / 1.43L PQBL. The latter references also appear for M24/M21; the locally held copy labelled M24 1.43 has no identified donor and does not by itself establish an SP BIOS.
product.olivetti-m24sp.technical.verifie: BluMach mentions the M24 SP as an alias of the M24 model. This reference has been checked in the code; the loader requests BIOS 1.44. It documents the existing implementation without demonstrating a 10 MHz SP configuration.
product.olivetti-m24sp.technical.limitat: The sheet does not yet allow an M24 SP to be created. A physical SP unit’s BIOS must be identified and checked, timing, memory, jumpers and peripherals validated, and boot and reset tested. No firmware was executed during this research.
product.olivetti-m24sp.technical.source_: Olivetti, Personal Computer Pocket Service Guide, vol. I, pp. 1-1–1-4: boards, memory, BIOS revisions and jumpers.
Computerwoche, 11/10/1985, “Olivetti will weltweit Nummer zwei werden”: SICOB presentation and position in the range.
Computerwoche, 22/11/1985, “Olivetti-Mikro verfügbar”: availability and configuration in Austria.
Sperimentare, 06/1986, pp. 29–30: manufacturer, specifications and Italian price for the published configuration.
Computerwoche, 14/08/1986, “Voller Hauptspeicherausbau jetzt serienmäßig”: German offer and report of increased disk capacity.
Freakedenough, Olivetti M24SP IO Board, CC0 1.0: interior photograph of one unit with installed cards; it does not define factory equipment.
BluMach 88f74ba3, machine_table.c and m_xt_olivetti.c: M24 SP alias and M24 BIOS loader.
DOS ROM BIOS collection, olivetti_m24, 1.43 HIGH/LOW: files labelled M24, with no physical donor identified as an SP.
